notes:
I don't have any notes on Esther 6 for you. My research tools stopped working before I could read a single source page.

**What happened:**
- I tried to open five verse-by-verse commentaries:
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/esther-6/
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/esther-6-commentary
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/esther/6.htm
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/esther/6.htm
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/esther/6.htm
- The first attempt failed because of a bug in my code. When I tried again, the system said I had used up my tool calls for this turn. My other tools can't reach the internet, so I couldn't search or open any other page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything from memory, not even the standard readings (such as the king's sleepless night as God's hidden providence, or Zeresh's warning in v. 13).

**What I can do next time:** If you send the request again, I'll start with the five commentaries above. Then I'll look for:
- **Different Protestant traditions:** Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition (Reformed), Desiring God and Spurgeon (Baptist), Wesley's notes at wesley.nnu.edu (Methodist), and 1517.org (Lutheran).
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes at netbible.org and bibleodyssey.org (modern scholarship), and newadvent.org and catholic.com (Catholic). The Catholic sites may cover the Greek additions to Esther, which some Bibles include and which bear on this chapter.

I'll write the notes verse by verse, with a URL after each point, and leave out anything I can't find.
